Base 2027 Kia EV9 Becomes More Expensive by Just $90; Some Upgrades Only Come for the Middle Grades
8 photos
Photo: Kia
Kia America has announced that it doesn't care too much about inflation for this year's Kia EV9 all-electric flagship, but the updates are also minor, unfortunately.
The US division of the South Korean automaker announced at the start of the month that its best-ever month of September was this year, with 77k deliveries, jumping 18%. There was also a great third-quarter sales tally of almost 237k vehicles, growing by eight percentage points.
Electrified models did great, especially hybrids, and Kia had no less than eight top-selling models: Seltos (+66 percent); Niro (+47 percent); K4 (+43 percent); Telluride (+42 percent); Sorento (+37 percent); Carnival (+21 percent); K5 (+15 percent); and Sportage (+10 percent).
Year-to-date, the company is at 667,386 sales, clearly topping last year’s 636,148, and now they are well on their way toward establishing a new full-year sales record. As such, the brand keeps upgrading its roster with announcements for the 2027 model year for pricing and details for various models like the Sorento, Sorento HEV and PHEV , the all-new base EV3 , or the mid-tier EV6.
Now it’s also the ripe time for the flagship EV9, of course, closing the trifecta of dedicated all-electric models . The 2026 Kia EV9 all-electric flagship has a starting MSRP of $54,900 sans destination for the Light RWD model, and the same configuration now costs just $90 more, plus the $1,645 for destination.
The 2026 Light Long Range RWD starts from $57,900 and also gets a premium of $90. On the other hand, the EV9 Wind AWD is $63,900 and will kick off at $64,090 (+$190), while the Land AWD is $68,900 and also becomes $69,990 due to the $190 hike.
Last but not least, the top GT-Line model goes back to the $90 hike, now costing $71,990 for the 2027 model year. That’s quite sensible, especially since the Wind gains black-finish 19-inch wheels and Glossy Black exterior touches plus the availability of the Wolf Gray exterior paint.
Additionally, the EV9 Land has the formerly optional Nightfall Edition Package as a standard perk, adding a torque boost from 379 lb.-ft. to 516 lb.-ft. and a dedicated interior color scheme with a black headliner and special stitching pattern on black synthetic leather seats.
According to Kia, “since its introduction, the all-electric three-row SUV has earned prestigious accolades, including 2024 North American Utility of the Year ™ and 2024 World Car of the Year, recognizing its distinctive design, spacious interior and advanced technology.”
The Light model has 215 or 201 hp for the Short or Long Range models, RWD, and 76.1 or 99.8 kWh batter packs. The latter is shared with the AWD Wind, Land, and GT-Line models, and they all have 379 hp. The best range is achieved by the Light LR with 305 miles on a charge.
